item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00494","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C25","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 is a direct and material drafting precursor concerning the same Peace Corps authorization. The child updates C16's original recruitment and deployment projections, repeats its legislative-transmittal and authorization framework, and adapts its appeal for initial enactment into an appeal for continuation and expansion. C25 supplies important underlying Peace Corps subject matter but is an executive order with materially different operative machinery. C18 has a weaker structural analogy involving congressional authorization to continue and expand an international service program.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am transmitting herewith, for the consideration of the Congress, legislation to enable continuation of the current Peace Corps program, and to make possible a further expansion of its work.","parent_excerpt":"I have the honor to transmit herewith for the consideration of the Congress a legislative proposal to authorize the establishment of a Peace Corps in fiscal year 1962","explanation":"The child reuses the earlier legislative-transmittal framework for the same program, changing the objective from establishment to continuation and expansion."},{"child_excerpt":"This legislation will permit the Peace Corps to have 6,700 volunteers in the field by June 30, 1963, compared to the maximum of 2,400 permitted under the present appropriation.","parent_excerpt":"This should enable the Peace Corps to have 500-1,000 volunteers abroad by the end of this calendar year, to have approximately 2,700 abroad or in training by June 1962","explanation":"Both justify authorization through concrete staged volunteer-strength projections; the child updates the earlier figures and timetable."},{"child_excerpt":"More than 20,000 Americans have volunteered to serve","parent_excerpt":"More than 8,500 Peace Corps Volunteer Questionnaires have been returned","explanation":"The child updates the earlier evidence of strong domestic participation as part of the same argument for congressional support."},{"child_excerpt":"I urge prompt consideration of the legislation authorizing an increase in the authorization to 63.75 million dollars for Peace Corps programs in fiscal year 1963","parent_excerpt":"This legislative proposal requests that Congress authorize $40 million for this program for the fiscal year 1962.","explanation":"The fiscal-year funding authorization and accompanying request for prompt congressional action are materially parallel, with revised amounts and dates."}]}
